title: California Issues Subpoena to Nvidia Over Chip Sales to China
description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued subpoenas to Nvidia and former CEO Jensen Huang regarding reports that they misled investors about advanced AI chips potentially reaching China. "The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said in a press release. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information -- and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law." The probe follows Huang's resignation amid allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy and comes as the SEC reportedly conducts a similar investigation. The Hill reports: Bonta's office said the information obtained through the subpoenas will help it to determine if Nvidia, which is based in Santa Clara, Calif., violated state law through its alleged actions. "Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta continued.
 
[...] Following the Huang scandal, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents Thursday showing the U.S. authorized the sale of nearly 900,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to Defense Department-designated Chinese military companies. An Nvidia spokesperson previously told The Hill, "The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." "Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China," the spokesperson added.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: White House Replaces Cyber Director After Tech Outages
description:
President Trump has named Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten A. Davies as his new national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross amid a broader shakeup of the administration's cybersecurity and AI leadership. According to Axios, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller pushed for Cairncross' removal over concerns about his technical qualifications. From the report: "Kirsten has the credentials to excel in this position and has already been Senate-confirmed," an administration official said. At the Pentagon, Davies has been the top adviser to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "on all matters relating to information management, information technology, cybersecurity, and information assurance," according to her bio.
 
Before serving in the Trump administration, Davies worked for Unilever and "led global cyber resilience for one of the world's largest consumer goods enterprises," her bio says. Davies' career also has included technology and cyber roles at Estee Lauder, Barclays-Africa Group, Hewlett Packard and Siemens. She founded the Institute for Cyber, a nonprofit organization dedicated to citizen safety and security in the digital universe. Trump is also filling other key cyber positions, notes Axios. "His pick for the top job at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which helps defend federal civilian networks and critical infrastructure, Palantir executive Michael LoSapio, faced a combative confirmation hearing Thursday."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Google Is Putting AI Chats Right On the Homepage
description:

Google's vice president of product, Robby Stein, says the company is rolling out the option because "people are coming to Search with more questions that aren't just one and done," adding that "in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web." The Verge reports: It's yet another big change for Google's homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.

title: UK Government Forced To Disclose Secret Apple Backdoor Order
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from TechCrunch: The U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information. The Thursday ruling from the U.K.'s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret. The tribunal's ruling rejected the Home Office's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security. [...] A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year. The order follows a year-long dispute that began when British authorities reportedly sought a backdoor to users' data worldwide, drawing criticism from U.S. lawmakers over privacy concerns. Rather than comply, Apple disabled its Advanced Data Protection feature for U.K. users and challenged the order in court.
 
The government later narrowed its demand to British nationals' data, prompting another legal challenge from Apple.
 
Apple said it welcomes the ruling to make public the fact that the U.K. Home Office issued a technical capability notice, reiterating that it has "never built a backdoor or master key" to its products or services and "never will."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Beyls: Wrapping up LLVM's relicensing effort
description:
Kristof Beyls has published
a summary to the LLVM discussion forum to announce that the project is
declaring success and bringing its relicensing
effort to a close after eight years.


We've been asking past contributors to relicense their work since 2018. New
contributions have come in under Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception since January
19, 2019. Code contributed before that date was under LLVM's earlier licenses
(UIUC/NCSA, plus MIT for some runtime libraries), so we needed permission from
its authors to move it over. [...]

Today, more than 99.5% of all lines of code ever contributed to LLVM are
either covered by the new license, too small for copyright to apply, or no
longer in the repository.


Rather than trying to "chase the last tiny fraction forever" LLVM is
winding up the effort. Any contributors with code contributed before January 19,
2019 who have not signed a relicensing agreement and do not want their
contributions made available under Apache-2.0 with the LLVM-exception can still
reach out to the project to ensure their code has the appropriate SPDX license
identifier.

description:
Intuit has agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, less than one-third of the $12 billion it paid to acquire the email-marketing platform in 2021. The deal is set to close in early 2027. CNBC reports: In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing.
 
Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue. While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.

title: Google Signs Deal With Blue Origin to Send Satellite Data Centers Into Orbit
description:
Google has partnered with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch satellite-based AI data centers into orbit as part of its experimental Project Suncatcher initiative. "Engadget reports: Each of these satellites will be equipped with "roughly the capacity of a data center rack" and will enter into a sun-synchronous orbit via heavy-lift New Glenn rockets. The rocket will carry several Google tensor processing units, the company's proprietary AI chips, along with data center servers. The first launch isn't scheduled until early 2029, so we have a couple of years to see if this whole project even works.
 
This is an experiment that Google calls a "long-term moonshot" to see if it's possible to put AI infrastructure in space by "tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit." The benefits of this would be massive. Data centers here on Earth are notorious hogs, with their snouts all over electricity grids, land and cooling systems. The hope is that the harsh vacuum of the cosmos will be a better fit for the technology.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Amazon Fights the Delivery Protection Act With Homepage Banner, In-App Pop-Up
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a New York City bill. When I log into Amazon today, I'm met with a vertical banner that reads: "ATTENTION NYC Council could add up to $5 per order" with a button that says "Act now." The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn't specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I'm logged into Amazon.
 
Amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 (518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses. Clicking on "Act now" on Amazon's homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states: "Right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees." The move marks an unusual expansion of Amazon's political advocacy, reports Ars, and raises concerns about the company's ability to influence shoppers and present a one-sided view of legislation.
 
The bill, which also affects companies like FedEx and DoorDash, remains stalled in a City Council committee, with no vote scheduled.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Iowans Brace For Lead Dust Cloud As Army Plans to Detonate 5 Tons of Bomb-Making Chemicals
description:
The U.S. Army plans to detonate roughly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Friday. "The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground," an advisory states. "Lead is toxic to humans and animals. The goal of this advisory is to provide the public with actionable information out of an abundance of caution to minimize lead exposure." PBS reports: Officials have released maps showing the potential drift north, and the Army will continue to update the maps based on weather. Some schools in the region have already canceled classes. Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but thousands more could be affected. The vibrations from the two blasts will be quick but could break old windows in town. The resulting dust is expected to linger for no more than one hour, depending on wind speed, officials said. While the Army recommends cleaning cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces, residents have taken to social media to voice concern and question whether that will be enough.
 
[...] Middletown residents learned in March that the Army needed to dispose of several dozen barrels containing lead azide, after the ammunition plant paused operations as part of a review and the degraded material was discovered. "The safety of our people and our neighbors is non-negotiable," Lt. Col. Daniel Nosse, commander of the plant, said at the time, acknowledging the volatility of the chemical compound used in munitions production. The Army shared more details during a public meeting in Middletown in October, advising that a detonation was planned for an unspecified date in November.






Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Nvidia Approaches Arm Boss Rene Haas In Search For New CEO
description:
Nvidia has reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as it searches for a replacement for co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned last week amid a personal scandal. According to Bloomberg, Haas is emerging as a leading contender for the job. The 64-year-old previously worked at Nvidia as general manager of its computing products business before joining Arm, giving him firsthand experience with the AI chip giant. The Guardian reports: Heidrick & Struggles, the recruiting firm hired by the company's board, has started contacting potential candidates, according to Bloomberg. It reported that Rene Haas, who joined Arm in 2013 and became chief executive in 2022, is among those approached. [...] Haas, 64, is viewed as the leading contender for the top job at Nvidia, having previously worked at the $3.6tn company for seven years as the general manager of its computing products.
 
Reports suggest that other potential candidates include: Ian Buck, an Nvidia vice-president; Lisa Su, AMD's chief executive; and Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer. Arm, which is listed in New York but retains its global headquarters in Cambridge, has about 500 users of its chip designs worldwide, including Nvidia, Apple, Samsung and Qualcomm. The company employs more than 7,000 staff, including more than 3,000 in the UK. It is the biggest tech firm headquartered in Britain, now valued at $196bn. Haas told a tech conference in Austin on Wednesday that Huang was "a legend." "What he built at Nvidia is historic," he said. "You don't have many champions like that."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Disclose Cyberattack On Third-Party Vendors
description:
JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed cyberattacks involving third-party service providers that exposed customer marketing data, including names, email addresses and, in some cases, phone numbers and postal codes. All three companies said their core systems or payment networks were unaffected, while JPMorgan emphasized that the incident was unrelated to the banking disruptions earlier this week. Reuters reports: A cyber extortion group called "n0n" claimed on November 16 to have obtained cardmember engagement records that included "hundreds of thousands of campaign interactions for tens of thousands of distinct cardmember email addresses," according to a screenshot of the message captured by cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The data includes what appears to be 124 bank employee email addresses and more than 16,000 customer email addresses, some with phone numbers and postal codes, according to a Reuters review. Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the data.
 
The same hacking group on November 16 posted similar claims regarding Visa and Mastercard and posted data. [...] The Mastercard data posted by n0n includes marketing data related to customers in North America, the Middle East and Africa, and a small number of Mastercard employee email addresses. The hacking group has claimed roughly 200 incidents since emerging in September 2026, according to eCrime.ch. "Customers don't distinguish between a bank and a vendor when it comes to a cyberattack, so there is a question of reputational risk here," said Carissa Robb at SolomonEdwards, a consulting firm. "There needs to be a little bit more pressure on how often companies are scrutinizing the amount of data that is shared with vendors and the necessity of the data being shared," Robb said.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: PHP Readies Critical Security Updates to Patch Another RCE Flaw
description:
PHP has released security updates addressing seven critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities across its supported versions, just four weeks after patches for the widely exploited PHP2Shell flaws. SecurityWeek reports: One of the security defects expected to be resolved is CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution (RCE) defect in the file-upload progress tracking functionality. The vulnerability was publicly disclosed two days after PHP2Shell made headlines. PHP's maintainers warned at the time that the security flaw can be triggered only under an unusual combination of configuration and code.
 
"An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled," PHP said last month. Noting that patches would be released as part of the regular update cycle, PHP developers recommended disabling session upload, a setting also listed as a mitigation for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two RCE bugs tracked as PHP2Shell.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Google Will Launch Android App Verification Requirement Globally In January 2027
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: Google announced Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon.
 
The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps.
 
In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months." So far, Google is getting what it wanted from this initiative, with "millions" of non-Play apps already registered. The company says this accounts for more than 99 percent of global Android app installs.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Palo Alto Networks Signs $4.5 Billion Deal For Applied Compute
description:
Palo Alto Networks has agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion as it expands beyond traditional cybersecurity into securing enterprise AI systems, including the training and deployment of open-weight models. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Reuters reports: Palo Alto Networks has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, with recent deals, including its $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi. The company is looking to tap growing cybersecurity spending as the rapid adoption of AI creates new security risks and gives attackers new ways to exploit vulnerabilities.
 
"AI tools are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than companies can patch them, and that is pushing customers to consolidate onto fewer platforms," said Catharine Trebnick, senior research analyst at Rosenblatt Securities. With the acquisition of Applied Compute, Palo Alto aims to offer a technology platform that helps customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their use of AI.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Anthropic Tops $2 Trillion Market Cap After IPO Debut
description:
Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest initial public offering in history. Shares opened at $111.50, a 34% premium that briefly pushed the Claude developer's market capitalization above $2 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable companies. CNBC reports: The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year.
 
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI, now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced a sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. [The Pentagon formally designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk in March following a dispute over military use of its AI models.]





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: [$] Added indirection allows for larger BPF programs
description:
The BPF verifier has historically worked by tracing every possible path of
execution through a program, checking, at each instruction, that various safety
properties hold. This works, but it can result in an exponential increase in the
number of states that need checking in programs with complicated control-flow.
Alexei Starovoitov, one of the kernel's core BPF maintainers, has shared

a patch set that substantially reworks how the verifier tracks states, in
order to reduce the size of that exponential explosion.

title: Gamers Skip Work to Play GTA VI After 13-Year Wait
description:
After a 13-year wait, Rockstar games' Grand Theft Auto VI has officially (and finally) launched today to near-universal acclaim, earning a 99/100 score on Metacritic and generating an estimated $1.84 billion from 19 million copies sold. The highly anticipated release has prompted gamers to take time off work, attracted nearly 2 million concurrent Twitch viewers, and sparked celebrations around the world. "Video game critics have lauded it, describing it as a 'masterpiece' and 'the single most impressive video game' they've ever played," reports NBC News.
 
An expert told Reuters that there could be a "work blackout across the board." Another expert suggested that $1 billion in U.S. productivity could be lost as people take time off to play the game, which is estimated to take about 50 hours to complete.
 
Here's a roundup of GTA VI reviews:

 IGN (10/10) calls it "the single most impressive video game I have ever played." GameSpot (10/10) praises its extraordinary attention to detail, calling it a culmination of Rockstar's open-world achievements. Push Square (10/10) describes it as Rockstar's deepest and most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2, though it notes the 30fps cap and occasional pacing issues. Eurogamer (5/5) praises its ambitious world and the emotional depth of Jason and Lucia's relationship. Digital Foundry highlights its groundbreaking visual realism, ray tracing, and simulation detail, while acknowledging compromises from the 30fps target. Bloomberg calls it an all-time classic, praising the unpredictable interactions and remarkable freedom of exploration.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

query performance with the new pg_plan_advice extension, and a number
of performance improvements.

In September, LWN covered the
removal of several features initially slated for this release. See the release notes for
a full list of new features and changes.
